records.title: Vault admission: allowlist widened, but no .xpt/.zip/.pptx, a 50 MB in-memory cap, and extraction/OCR/chunking still run inside the request
records.evidenceAtHead: shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-38: the Vault list is now .pdf .docx .xlsx .txt .md .csv .tsv .json .xml .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .doc .xls .rtf. Still absent: .xpt, .sas7bdat, .zip, .pptx. Grep for xpt finds no upload path, only the eCTD/STF validators. :46 VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 50*1024*1024. server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:55 MAX_FILE_SIZE = VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES ('unchanged 50 MB'). :69-80 multer.memoryStorage() with limits.fileSize. server/services/storage/storage-provider.ts:20,51: put() takes a Buffer, and get() returns one. server/services/vault/vault-ingest.service.ts:381-404: pdfPageCount and extractDocumentText (OCR) are awaited inside the request. :715-718: chunkDocumentForIngest is awaited after commit, and it embeds over the network when ana.vault_chunking is on. OCR has no concurrency limit (server/services/ocr/*). terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 idle_timeout = 60. Compared against 92ccdba1:server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:53-56, which had the 9-extension list, 50 MB and memoryStorage.
records.fixedBy: 10222a024 (shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-38): the allowlist was widened to .tsv/.json/.xml (so define.xml is admitted) and to .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif, with byte checks in server/utils/fileSignature.ts:45-64,134-150. 13efb8fca: one 50 MB cap shared by Vault and Data Room (no increase).
records.remaining:
1. SAS transport datasets (.xpt), .zip and .pptx are refused with 400 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED.
2. Anything over 50 MB is refused with 413.
3. The whole file is buffered in memory three times over: multer memoryStorage, the Buffer-based storage put(), and the Buffer AV scan.
4. Text extraction, OCR and passage chunking (plus optional embedding) run synchronously inside the HTTP request. Behind the 60 s ALB idle timeout, a long OCR can return 504 while the ingest continues on the server.
5. Concurrent large or scanned uploads can exhaust the memory of one Fargate task.
records.severityRationale: An FDA IND for a small biotech normally carries SEND datasets (.xpt plus define.xml) for nonclinical studies that started after Dec 2017 (FDA Data Standards Catalog). define.xml is now admitted, but .xpt is not, so the pilot cannot hold or file its Module 4/5 datasets in the platform. Large report PDFs over 50 MB are refused. This is not P0: PDF and DOCX, the bulk of IND content, upload, and datasets can be handled outside the platform with founder support.
records.humanTestingNote:
Symptoms:
- The Vault file picker does not offer .xpt, .zip or .pptx. Choosing one anyway returns 'File type .xpt is not allowed. Accepted: …' (400).
- A file over 50 MB returns 'The file exceeds the 50 MB ingest limit.' (413).
- A large scanned PDF keeps the upload spinner running while it is OCR'd in the request. On staging behind the ALB this can end in a 504 even though the document was admitted. Refresh the Vault before retrying, or the retry may be treated as a re-upload or next version.

Workaround: test with text-layer PDFs and DOCX under 50 MB, and keep datasets outside the Vault.
records.instructions:
1. File types. In shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-33, add vault:true entries:
   - '.xpt': textExtraction 'none', byteCheckSupported true, chat false, limitation 'SAS V5 transport; stored and hashed, not parsed'.
   - '.pptx': textExtraction 'none'.
   - '.zip': only if the founder confirms zipped content belongs in the Vault.
   In server/utils/fileSignature.ts, add signature checks: XPT V5 starts with the ASCII 'HEADER RECORD*******LIBRARY HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!' at offset 0; PPTX is ZIP magic PK\x03\x04 plus a presentationml content type (the MIME is already in the list at :64); ZIP is PK\x03\x04. Bind each MIME to its extension in verifyDeclaredTypeForName. Add a unit test asserting that every vault:true format has byteCheckSupported true, and show it failing by adding a format without a check.
2. Disk buffering. In server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:69-80, replace multer.memoryStorage() with multer.diskStorage into a per-request temp dir under os.tmpdir(). Unlink in a finally block on every outcome, including 4xx. Raise VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES (shared constant :46) to the founder-chosen ceiling (for example 1 GB). Keep CHAT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES equal, or document why they differ, because 13efb8fca made them one cap on purpose.
3. Streaming storage. Add putStream({orgId, programId, filename, mime, stream}) to IStorageProvider (server/services/storage/storage-provider.ts:51). Implement it in s3-provider.ts with @aws-sdk/lib-storage Upload (multipart), computing SHA-256 while streaming, and in local-provider.ts with stream.pipeline to a file. Keep put(Buffer) for small callers. ingestVaultDocument takes a file path and uses putStream.
4. AV on files. Add scanFile/scanStream to server/utils/virusScan.ts (INSTREAM chunks from a read stream), and let assertUploadSafe (server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts) take a path. Keep it fail-closed in production. Set clamd StreamMaxLength at or above the new cap (ties to CAT1-01).
5. Async extraction. In server/services/vault/vault-ingest.service.ts, move :381-404 (pdfPageCount, extractDocumentText) and :708-718 (chunkDocumentForIngest) out of the request:
   - Commit the document with processing_status 'PENDING' (already written at :527) and a catalog extraction outcome of 'pending'.
   - Process it in a worker: bull is already a dependency at package.json:542, or use a DB-polled sweep modelled on server/services/vault/document-chunking-backfill.service.ts:147 backfillVaultChunks.
   - The worker reads the bytes from storage, extracts, updates extracted_text/page_count/word_count/processing_status ('EXTRACTED' or 'EXTRACTION_FAILED' with the reason) through recordExtractionOutcome, then chunks.
   - Confirm that the VR-06 immutability trigger on vault.documents permits these columns. If it does not, amend the creating migration in place with a dated header note (Rule 1); do not append.
6. Concurrency. Add a per-process semaphore (2 to 4) around OCR in server/services/ocr/index.ts.
7. Honest state. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Vault.tsx, show 'Reading…' for PENDING and the stated failure for EXTRACTION_FAILED, never an empty excerpt. Full-text and passage search results state how many documents are still being read.
8. Verify every gate failing first: run each acceptance test on HEAD, record the red, then implement.
records.acceptance:
1. A valid SAS V5 .xpt uploads with 201 and downloads with an X-Content-SHA256 equal to its source hash. A PE executable renamed .xpt gets 400 from the signature check. Both tests are red on HEAD (the first gets 400 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED).
2. A 200 MB PDF uploads with 201 using the local provider, and process RSS grows by less than 64 MB during the request. Red on HEAD (413).
3. A 300-page image-only PDF upload returns in under 5 s with processingStatus 'PENDING', and the worker then sets 'EXTRACTED' with page_count 300 and passages indexed. Red on HEAD, where the response waits for OCR.
4. Under NODE_ENV=production, an EICAR file still gets 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED, and with clamd stopped the upload gets 503.
5. The temp dir is empty after success, after a 4xx and after a 5xx.
records.dependencies: CAT1-01 (a deployed clamd sized for large streams). A founder decision on the size ceiling and on whether .zip is admitted. Infra: S3 multipart permissions on the task role.

records.title: Projects still have no membership or project roles: reads are org-wide, and program mutations are lead-or-manager only
records.evidenceAtHead: server/services/c2c/program-access.ts:22-28 header: 'READ ROUTES ARE NOT GATED … There is no membership store for uuid-keyed programs'. :58-65: canMutateProgram returns true only for org manage roles or lead_user_id. server/routes/c2c/projects.ts:603-640: GET / filters only on organization_id. :463-480: allowProgramMutation, used at :1326, :1353, :1521, :2098. :1185-1260: GET /:id/team returns the lead plus free-text team_members names with user_id null. :1190-1197: project_members cannot key a uuid program. Also gated on lead-or-manager: submission-service.ts:440 (anchor submission) and document-data-disposition/service.ts:69. Grep for regulatory_program_members|program_members across server, shared and migrations returns no hits. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Projects.tsx:222-225: `const [team] = useState<string[]>([])`. :707-712: 'Team assignment isn't available yet'. server/routes/concept2cure.ts:1902-2042: the sharing/members API on the integer projects.id space. Grep of client/src for '/sharing' returns nothing. project-vault.ts read routes (:1101 org-wide search, :1134, :1567, :1647-1793, :2117, :2183, :2281, :2294) carry no membership gate. Mitigations that are not a fix: org-level roles admin/approver/manager/reviewer/member/viewer with invitations (shared/constants/org-roles.ts:33; server/routes/tenant-users.ts; ddc8c0db5), and per-document authoring grants (doc_permissions).
records.remaining:
All of it:
- There is no project membership table, no project invitations and no project-level roles.
- Every org member reads every project and its Vault.
- Only the lead or an org manager/approver/admin can pin or unpin evidence, adopt, or anchor a submission. A member-role author who is not the lead is refused.
- The legacy concept2cure sharing API is still a parallel, uncalled path.
records.severityRationale: The pilot is a single invited small biotech in its own tenant. Tenant isolation (D3) holds. Org-wide visibility inside one sponsor is acceptable, and org-level reviewer/approver roles and per-document authoring grants exist. Lead-or-manager mutation is workable by giving the pilot's core users the manager or approver role. This becomes P1 for any CRO or multi-sponsor tenant, or a customer that requires need-to-know. Project-designated approvers would build on it, but CAT1-07 can be fixed without it.
records.humanTestingNote:
Symptoms:
- The New project wizard and Project home say 'Team assignment isn't available yet'.
- The Team panel lists only the lead (and any typed names, which are not linked to an account).
- Every org member sees every project and its Vault; there is no way to restrict a project.
- A tester with the 'member' org role who is not the project lead gets 403 when pinning or unpinning evidence, adopting, or anchoring a submission to the project.

Workaround: in Admin Access, give testers the manager or approver role (with a reason), or have the project lead perform those actions.
records.acceptance:
1. With visibility 'members', a same-org non-member gets 404 on GET /api/c2c/projects/:id, the project's Vault document list and download, and its authoring documents. The project does not appear in the list or in the org-wide Vault search. Red on HEAD.
2. A member with the author role, who is not the lead, can POST /:id/evidence. Red on HEAD (403).
3. Membership add, remove and re-role each require a reason and produce one chained audit row in the same transaction.
4. The concept2cure sharing/members routes are deleted, and the commit names the replacement.
5. The new table has organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, an RLS policy after deploy, and passes ci:migration-set-order.
records.dependencies: Founder decision on default visibility and the role set. CAT1-11 (project id-space convergence) before deleting the integer-id sharing API.

records.title: Authoring approval: a document's author can still approve it with one signature, and no review is required
records.remaining: Authoring /e-sign and /sign still let the document's creator (OWNER grant) or any global admin with a signing role approve and freeze alone. No REVIEWER signature or completed review is required before APPROVER. There is no multi-approver option, and the platform's canonical separation-of-duties check is not applied to Authoring.
records.severityRationale: A GxP pilot's QMS SOPs and its auditor expect four-eyes approval of controlled regulatory documents. The platform's own policy (separation-of-duties.ts header: adopted 'for every review/approval/lock', 'un-disableable') is violated by the approval path of a launch app, and P-18 tells the customer the opposite. This is not P0: signatures are re-verified, attributable and hash-bound; the Vault copy will not carry a self-approval; and the pilot can run under a two-person SOP in the meantime.
records.humanTestingNote:
Symptoms:
- A tester with an admin, approver or reviewer org role who created a document can open E-sign, choose Approval and sign. The document immediately becomes APPROVED and frozen, with one signature and no review.
- Filing that document to the Vault then reports that the Authoring approval was not carried (the author signed), so Authoring says Approved while the Vault version is unapproved.

Workaround: run the approval journey with separate accounts (author with the member role, reviewer, approver) and log self-approval acceptance as a known defect.
records.instructions:
1. Model authorship. In server/services/governance/separation-of-duties.ts, add an 'authoring-document' case to resolveTargetAuthors (:327). The authors are:
   - authoring_documents.created_by (WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2);
   - UNION DISTINCT doc_revisions.created_by, joined through authoring_sections s ON s.id = r.section_id AND s.doc_id = $1 AND r.tenant_id = $2 (include origin 'genesis', which is the creator; exclude 'platform-generated');
   - the actor recorded when an AI draft was accepted (authoring_ai_draft_candidates), if that column exists.
   Cast ids to integer. Show a lookup failure throwing (503 path) in a unit test.
2. Enforce in the routes.
   - In POST /docs/:docId/e-sign (authoring.router.ts:5294), after the meaning validation and before reverifyAuthoringSigner (:5332), call assertSignerIsNotAuthor(`authoring-document:${docId}`, tenantId, Number(getActorId(req)), { command: 'sign', meaning: meaning === 'APPROVER' ? 'approval' : meaning === 'REVIEWER' ? 'review' : 'authorship' }).
   - Map the errors exactly as server/routes/document-lifecycle.ts:251 does: SeparationOfDutiesError → 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES, AuthorUnresolved → 409, Unverified → 503.
   - Repeat the call inside the BEGIN block with { client } to close the race.
   - Apply the same in POST /docs/:docId/sign (:7373) and, for meaning REVIEWER, in POST /docs/:docId/freeze (:5019).
3. Required review. When meaning === 'APPROVER', and in /sign when the step clears the last workflow step, refuse with 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED (nothing written) unless, inside the transaction:
   (a) an authoring_signatures row exists with meaning 'REVIEWER' for this doc and content_hash = the current docHash, signed by someone who is neither the approver nor in the author set; and
   (b) no authoring_reviews row for the doc has review_status 'pending'.
   Extract this predicate from server/services/regulatory/authoring-approval-carryover.ts (the same rules: a reviewer covers D, signed no later than the approval, by a different person, neither is the author) into one exported function used by both, so there is no duplication. Then rewrite that file's header at :44-45.
4. Optional per-org tightening (admin may only tighten): an organization setting min_authoring_approvers, default 1. The APPROVED flip happens only on the Nth distinct APPROVER signature over the same docHash.
5. Tell the user before the dialog. In callerDocumentAccess (authoring.router.ts:1636-1745), fold the SoD and review-required decisions into `esign`, so DocumentWorkbench and AuthoringFilingBar (:145-148) withhold Approval and show the reason. The server stays the enforcement point.
6. After the code lands, correct the P-18 text in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md to match. Do not edit it before.
7. Failing-first tests (pglite or tests/db with three users holding signing roles):
   (a) the creator with the admin role signs APPROVER → 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES (red on HEAD: 200 and APPROVED);
   (b) a non-author approver with no REVIEWER signature → 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED (red on HEAD);
   (c) the reviewer also signing APPROVER → 403;
   (d) author signs AUTHOR, a reviewer signs REVIEWER, a third person signs APPROVER → APPROVED and frozen, and file-to-vault carries the approval.
   Run npm run ci:sign-ceremony.
records.acceptance:
1. On a document created by user A (admin role), A's APPROVER e-sign returns 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES, and the document status, authoring_signatures and frozen_documents are unchanged. Red on HEAD.
2. User B (approver role, not an author) signing APPROVER before any REVIEWER signature on the current hash returns 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED. Red on HEAD.
3. After C (reviewer) signs REVIEWER, B's APPROVER succeeds, and file-to-vault reports the approval carried.
4. The same refusals apply on /docs/:docId/sign.
5. The E-sign dialog does not offer Approval to the author, and shows the server's reason.
records.dependencies: None blocking. CAT1-06 is needed only if approvers are to be designated per project. Test fixtures need at least three users with signing roles (P-18 approver/reviewer assignment exists).

records.title: The editor's AI draft still retrieves org-wide Data Room atoms and never reads the project's Vault
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/authoring.router.ts:3785-3893 POST /sections/:sectionId/ai/draft calls embeddingService.searchHybrid(searchQuery, { limit: 5, organizationUuid: orgUuid, minSemanticScore: 0.65 }) at :3842-3846. It passes no projectId, and the block is byte-identical to 92ccdba1:3233-3237. The section query (:3796-3802) does not read authoring_documents.client_program_id. server/services/enhancedEmbeddingService.ts:524-600 searches lumen_data_atoms only. Its project filter (:574-578) is unused and keyed on the integer concept2cure_artifacts.project_id, not the program uuid. Vault ingest writes vault.document_chunks (vault-ingest.service.ts:708-718; document-chunking.service.ts:295-307) and never lumen_data_atoms; the only atom writers are chat/upload, c2c/knowledge-sources, projects/contextual-ingest and the CSR adapter. Attribution resolves only cre_evidence_sources through lumen source_id (authoring.router.ts:4015-4053). The client copy is untrue: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AuthoringAiDraft.tsx:573 says 'Retrieves evidence from this project's Data Room'. The canonical project-scoped Vault passage search already exists: server/services/vault/document-passage-search.ts:217 searchDocumentPassages({organizationId, organizationUuid, query}, {programId}), which returns pageNumber. AnA uses it (server/services/ana/document-passage-tools.ts:133-139), and since 1d5de6ca6 passages are indexed on every ingest without a flag or key.
records.remaining:
All of the impact remains:
- A document uploaded to the project's Vault is never retrieved or cited by the editor's AI draft.
- Retrieval spans every project in the org, so a draft for program A can cite program B's Data Room uploads.
- Two retrieval stacks persist: the editor uses lumen atoms, AnA uses Vault passages.
The pre-audit tenant scoping (organizationUuid) and the 1d5de6ca6 always-on passage index are enablers, not a fix.
records.severityRationale: 'AI drafting with citations to Vault evidence' is a core Authoring launch journey. Citing another program's material inside one sponsor is a data-integrity problem for a regulatory draft. The UI tells the user the evidence is project-scoped when it is not. This is not P0: there is no cross-tenant leak (org-scoped), retrieval status is reported honestly (ok/empty/failed), attributions resolve only to retrieved sources, and the AnA drafting path is grounded in the project's Vault.
records.humanTestingNote:
Requires a configured AI provider.

Symptoms:
- A tester uploads a study report to the project's Vault, opens a section in the editor and clicks 'Draft <section> from Data Room sources'. The draft reports that no Data Room source met the relevance threshold (not grounded), or it cites chat/Data Room uploads from any project in the organisation. The Vault upload is never cited.
- Citations never show a Vault document or page.

Workaround: ask AnA, in the open project, to draft the section (its passage search reads the project's Vault), then send it to the editor through the canvas.
records.instructions:
1. Project. In authoring.router.ts, add `to_jsonb(d)->>'client_program_id' AS program_id` to the section query (:3796-3802). If program_id is null, set retrievalStatus 'failed' with retrievalError 'This document is not in a project, so no project evidence could be retrieved', and do not fall back to an org-wide search (fail closed).
2. One retrieval path. Replace the searchHybrid block (:3832-3846) with searchDocumentPassages({ organizationId: tenantId, organizationUuid: orgUuid, query: searchQuery }, { limit: 5, programId: section.program_id }) from server/services/vault/document-passage-search.ts.
   - Map each hit to retrievedChunks { content: hit.text, title: hit.documentTitle, vaultDocumentId: hit.documentId, pageNumber: hit.pageNumber, chunkIndex: hit.chunkIndex }.
   - PassageSearchUnavailableError → 'failed' with its message.
   - No hits → 'empty', with the coverage note (indexed / total, unfiled Data Room uploads) carried in the draft metadata.
3. Evidence block (:3858-3870). Render each source as `[SRC-n] "<title>", p. <page>` (omit the page when it is null).
4. Attribution to Vault documents. Make the draft candidate and accept path (authoring.router.ts:4015-4075; services/clinical-regulatory-evidence/draft-candidate-store.ts; POST /sections/:sectionId/ai/draft/accept at :4142) carry a Vault reference: document id, version, page and chunk index. Either:
   (a) register one cre_evidence_sources row per Vault document version at ingest (source_type 'vault_document', metadata.vaultDocumentId) and resolve it like the existing link forms in retrieval-source-link.ts:61; or
   (b) add a nullable vault_document_id/page column to the candidate source table, in a new additive migration or by amending its creating migration in place with a dated note (Rule 1).
   The accept gate must still refuse an id that was not retrieved.
5. Zero duplication. Remove the lumen-atom retrieval from this route in the same change. Data Room captures reach the Vault through VR-11a filing; unfiled captures are reported in coverage, not searched silently. If the founder wants unfiled uploads included, route them through ragRouter (one router), not a second path.
6. Client. In AuthoringAiDraft.tsx (:156-193 messages, :533, :565, :573), say 'this project's Vault', and show document and page for each source.
7. Founder. Decide whether ana.vault_chunking (embeddings, which sends text to the provider) is on for pilot tenants. Keyword passage search works without it.
8. Failing-first tests (pglite or tests/db): see the acceptance criteria. Run each on HEAD first and record the red.
records.acceptance:
1. Program A has an authoring document. A PDF containing a unique phrase is uploaded to A's Vault. Drafting the matching section returns retrievalStatus 'ok', and a source names that Vault document id and a page number. Red on HEAD ('empty' or atoms only).
2. A Data Room/chat upload containing the phrase is made to program B only. Drafting in A retrieves nothing from B. Red on HEAD, which searches all org atoms.
3. A document with no client_program_id gets retrievalStatus 'failed', and no evidence block is sent to the model.
4. Accepting the draft records span attribution to the Vault document and page, and an attribution to a document that was not retrieved is refused.
5. The route no longer calls enhancedEmbeddingService.searchHybrid (grep).
records.dependencies: A founder decision on Vault passage embeddings (cost and data placement). A configured, approved AI provider is needed to exercise it end to end (D4 model governance).
